title: Just like home
caption: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 2500, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 2500 · constellation Lynx · about 30 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Wispy spiral arms swirl out from a bright, elongated core in this Hubble image of NGC 2500. The galaxy is a barred spiral, and it sits roughly 30 million light-years from us, in the northern constellation Lynx. William Herschel discovered it more than 200 years ago.

Bars like this one are more common than astronomers once believed. Around two-thirds of all spiral galaxies have a straight bar cutting through the middle, the Milky Way among them. Bars are glowing nurseries for new stars and help channel material toward a galaxy's active core.

NGC 2500 is still forming stars, but unevenly. Its upper half, where the arms are a little better defined, holds far more star-forming regions than the lower half, and they show up as bright, dotted islands of light.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.77 x 2.56 arcminutes) and distance (30 million light years), the frame spans roughly 24,000 × 22,000 light-years. Its light set out about 30 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 and combines ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared filters. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, and the galaxy is far too faint to see in this detail without a large telescope.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: NGC 2500 also resembles our galaxy in its surroundings. The Milky Way belongs to the Local Group, a gathering of over 50 galaxies loosely bound by gravity. NGC 2500 is part of a similar group, the NGC 2841 group, whose members include NGC 2541, NGC 2537, NGC 2552 and a bright spiral resembling Andromeda, NGC 2481.
alt: A barred spiral galaxy with wispy arms swirling from a bright, elongated core, dotted with bright islands of light, mostly in its upper half.
